# C++

- **Write for a human reader first.** Names say what the thing is or does, unabbreviated (`flush_once`, not `fl1`; `has_pending_entry`, not `flag`). Read top-down, early `return` over nesting, a named intermediate over a dense expression. Headers and why-comments follow `docs.mdc`, as `//` lines above the first `#include` (clang-format keeps them: `ReflowComments: false`).
- **Layers are CMake targets; linking is the gate.** `domain` (pure types, rules, knobs in `config/`; the standard library only) ← `usecases` (use-cases + their ports) ← `adapters` (one per vendor, plus the system clock). Each target's public include directory is `cpp/<layer>/include`, so a layer can include only what it links. `cpp-layers.json` says which layers each row may link (`may`), which system families its code may not call (`deny`: io, clock, env, process, thread, random, net, dynamic), and which row may link third-party libraries (`anyLibrary`, adapters only). Widening a row is a decision, not a fix (`docs/ports-and-adapters.md`).
- **The checks read the build as evaluated, not the text.** CMake can add a flag, link, or include path from a dozen places (a preset, a toolchain file, `add_compile_options`, a source property), so `pnpm cpp:build` reads what CMake actually configured (File API: every target's links, include paths, sources, flags, standard, compiler) and what each unit really compiled and called:
  - a first-party target with no row, a row with no target, a link off its row (followed through a link cycle, which CMake reports as a chain), a third-party link on an inner row, a source outside the layer's directory, another layer's headers on its include path;
  - every header each unit included (`ninja -t deps`), so a `#include "../../adapters/…"` that dodges the include path is caught; and every `#include` in a layer's own files, judged by that file's layer (`stacks/cpp/sources.mjs`), so a domain header that includes an adapters one is caught even while only adapters includes it;
  - every symbol each layer's archive leaves undefined (`nm`), against its `deny` families (`getenv`, `std::chrono::system_clock::now`, `fopen`, `std::thread`, `random_device`, `socket`, `dlopen`, …), so a call through a typedef or a fully qualified name is seen as the linker sees it.
- **Warnings are errors, and nothing may turn them down.** `CPP_WARNINGS` in `CMakeLists.txt` is `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wold-style-cast -Wnon-virtual-dtor -Woverloaded-virtual -Wimplicit-fallthrough -Werror` (the floor is `REQUIRED_WARNINGS` in `stacks/cpp/evaluated.mjs`). The configured checks refuse, on any first-party target and from any source: a missing flag, `-Wno-error`, `-w` or `--no-warnings`, any `-Wno-*`, a flag that makes headers system ones (`-isystem…`, `--system-header-prefix`, `-iwithprefix…`), a first-party include directory marked `SYSTEM`, a non-C++ compile (a `.c` file escapes every flag check: name it `.cpp`), a standard below C++20, GNU extensions, a sanitizer dropped from the compile or the link, `-fsanitize-recover`, and an ignore list. The source rules refuse `#pragma … diagnostic`, `#pragma … system_header`, `#pragma warning`, `_Pragma`, `no_sanitize` in any spelling (`__no_sanitize__`, `no_sanitize_thread` …) and `disable_sanitizer_instrumentation`, `__asan_default_options` and friends, and `__lsan_disable`.
- **clang-tidy floor, clang-format layout.** `.clang-tidy` turns on bugprone, cert-err58, concurrency, cppcoreguidelines, misc, modernize, performance, readability (each switched-off check carries its reason there). `pnpm cpp:lint` forces `--warnings-as-errors=*` on the command line and checks each directory's evaluated config: every `REQUIRED_TIDY_CHECKS` check on (`stacks/cpp/sources.mjs`), every check the root turns on still on unless `cpp-layers.json` `"tidyOff"` lists it for that directory, and the options of those checks equal to the root's (a check `"tidyOff"` lists for a directory may differ there). So a nested `.clang-tidy` (which must say `InheritParentConfig: true`), its `CheckOptions`, or an emptied `WarningsAsErrors` can't switch one off quietly. A real exception is `// NOLINT(<check>): <why>` or `// NOLINTNEXTLINE(<check>): <why>` on the one line, naming each check (no globs); a bare NOLINT, one with no reason, and a NOLINTBEGIN without checks fail. clang-format (Google, 120 columns) owns layout: `clang-format -i <file>`; `// clang-format off` needs a reason on the same line.
- **Expected failures are values.** Return `domain::Outcome<T, E>` (`cpp/domain/include/domain/outcome.hpp`, `[[nodiscard]]`) with `E` an `enum class` or a `std::variant` of structs, handled by `std::visit` or an exhaustive `switch` (no `default:` over your own enum, so `-Wswitch` names a new case). Not `std::expected` yet: clang 18 can't compile libstdc++ 13's (`docs/deferred.md`). Throw only for a broken invariant. A port's contract names its failures; an adapter maps vendor errors to them.
- **Time and threads.** Wall-clock time and sleeping are ports (`WallClock`, `Sleeper`), so tests run on virtual time. A use-case may lock (`std::mutex`) but not start threads or sleep. The floor requires `thread` denied only in `domain`; the seed's `usecases` row denies it too, and a project that needs a worker thread there drops it from that one row on purpose.
- **Parse at the boundary.** Adapters turn bytes and rows into domain types; `domain` takes valid values.
- **Tools.** clang 18+ with clang-tidy and clang-format, cmake 3.28+, ninja; g++ 13+ for the second-compiler leg. On Linux, `bash stacks/cpp/install-tools.sh` adds the sanitizer runtimes (apt's `libclang-rt-18-dev`) and lowers `vm.mmap_rnd_bits` for TSan (both need sudo; a self-hosted runner has them installed by hand). A missing tool skips loudly locally and fails under `CI=true`; an old or broken one always fails. GoogleTest is fetched once per tree by `FetchContent`, pinned by URL and sha256 in `CMakeLists.txt`. Build trees live in `build-cpp/<preset>` (ignored). Presets: `asan` (clang, ASan+UBSan), `tsan` (clang, TSan), `gcc` (g++, CI only, or `CPP_PACK_GCC=1`).
- **The edit hook** (`stacks/cpp/check-edited.mjs`) runs the source rules, clang-format on the file, an incremental asan build with the layer checks, and clang-tidy on the unit (a header: on one unit that includes it), each under a named limit, and never reports a missing tool as clean.
- **Every gate is proved.** `pnpm cpp:gates` plants a violation of each rule (source rules, every configured-flag and link rule, an include reach, every denied family, the tidy floor and nested configs, format, a zero-test run, a test behind `#if 0`, an ASan, UBSan, LSan, and TSan report, each test property that turns a failure into a pass) in its own scratch copy and fails unless each is reported by name. Weakening a rule means editing the gates too, in the same reviewed diff. Locally they skip when nothing they read changed (`testing-cpp.mdc`).
- **What the gates are for:** making drift loud (an agent or contributor crossing a layer, a warning, or a test) and refusing settings that switch a gate off. They are not a sandbox against someone set on evading them; the classes they knowingly don't stop are in `docs/deferred.md` (C++ pack → what the gates don't stop).
- Layout: `cpp/domain/` (`include/config/` knobs, `include/domain/`, `src/`), `cpp/usecases/` (`include/usecases/<use-case>/`: use-case + `ports.hpp`), `cpp/adapters/`, `cpp/tests/` (`domain/`, `usecases/`, `chaos/` fixtures, `support/`). Namespaces follow the layers (`notes::config`, `notes::domain`, `notes::usecases`, `notes::adapters`); `notes` and the CMake project name `notesync` are placeholders.
